questions.q: An electron falls through a distance 1.5 cm in a uniform electric field of magnitude 2.0 × 10$^4$ N/C from rest. The time taken to cover this distance in second is _____. (e = 1.6 × 10$^{-19}$ C, m$_e$ = 9.11 × 10$^{-31}$ kg)

What will be the total electric flux through the faces of the cube as given in the figure with side of length 'a' if a charge Q is placed at B, midpoint of an edge of the cube (see figure)? [Figure: a cube of side a with a point charge Q placed at B, the midpoint of one edge of the cube]
questions.explanation: A charge placed on an edge of a cube is shared equally by the 4 cubes that meet along that edge, so the flux through one cube is $\dfrac{1}{4}\left(\dfrac{Q}{\epsilon_0}\right)=\dfrac{Q}{4\epsilon_0}$.

questions.q:
Consider three point charges $-2Q$, $Q$ and $-Q$ and three surfaces S$_1$, S$_2$ and S$_3$ as shown in the figure. Match the entries of List-I with that of List-II. [Figure: two overlapping circles inside a larger circle — the upper small circle (S$_1$) contains charge $-2Q$, the lower small circle (S$_2$) contains charge $-Q$, charge $Q$ sits at the boundary between S$_1$ and S$_2$ (inside both), and S$_3$ is the large outer circle enclosing all three charges]
List-I
(a) Net flux through S$_1$
(b) Net flux through S$_2$
(c) Net flux through S$_3$
List-II
(i) $\dfrac{-2Q}{\epsilon_0}$
(ii) $\dfrac{-Q}{\epsilon_0}$
(iii) Zero
Codes:
options: a - ii, b - i, c - iii
a - iii, b - ii, c - i
a - i, b - ii, c - iii
a - ii, b - iii, c - i
questions.explanation: By Gauss's law, flux depends only on the enclosed charge. S$_1$ encloses $-2Q$ and $Q$, net $-Q$, giving flux $-Q/\epsilon_0$ (ii). S$_2$ encloses $Q$ and $-Q$, net zero, giving zero flux (iii). S$_3$ encloses all three charges, net $-2Q$, giving flux $-2Q/\epsilon_0$ (i). So a-ii, b-iii, c-i.

questions.q:
An electric dipole of dipole moment $\vec P$ is placed in the uniform electric field $\vec E$. Then which of the following statements are correct?
Statement I: The torque on the dipole is $\vec P \times \vec E$
Statement II: The potential energy of the dipole is $-\vec P \cdot \vec E$
Statement III: The net force on the dipole is non zero
questions.explanation: Torque = $\vec P \times \vec E$ and potential energy = $-\vec P \cdot \vec E$ are correct; in a uniform field the net force on a dipole is zero, so Statement III is false.

questions.q: A metallic sphere of radius R carrying a charge q is kept at certain distance from another metallic sphere of radius R/4 carrying a charge Q. What is the electric flux at any point inside the metallic sphere of radius R due to the sphere of radius R/4?
questions.explanation: Inside the material of a conductor in electrostatic equilibrium the electric field is always zero, so the flux through any surface drawn inside it is zero, irrespective of external charges.

questions.q: You are given a dipole of charge + q and − q separated by a distance 2R. A sphere 'A' of radius 'R' passes through the centre of the dipole as shown below and another sphere 'B' of radius '2R' passes through the charge + q. Then the electric flux through the sphere A is [figure: concentric spheres A (radius R) and B (radius 2R) centred at −q; +q lies on the boundary of A]
questions.explanation: Sphere A (radius R, centred on −q) encloses only the charge −q, so by Gauss's law the flux through it is $-q/\varepsilon_0$.

questions.q: Charges are uniformly spread on the surface of a conducting sphere. The electric field from the centre of sphere to a point outside the sphere varies with distance r from the centre as [graphs of E vs r]
options: graph rising to a peak at r = R then decreasing (curve 1)
graph rising to a peak at r = R then decreasing more steeply (curve 2)
questions.explanation: For a charged conducting sphere, E = 0 inside, rises to a maximum at the surface (r = R), and falls off as $1/r^2$ outside — matching the second graph.

questions.q: Which of the following is a correct statement?
options: Gauss's law is true for any closed surface
Gauss's law is true for any open surface
Gauss's law is not applicable when charges are not symmetrically distributed over a closed surface.
Gauss's law does not hold good for a charge situated outside the Gaussian surface.
questions.explanation: Gauss's law, $\oint \vec E\cdot d\vec A=q_{enc}/\varepsilon_0$, holds for any closed surface regardless of the charge distribution or symmetry.

questions.q: A body has a charge of $-3.2\mu C$. The number of excess electrons it has is
questions.explanation: $n=\dfrac{Q}{e}=\dfrac{3.2\times10^{-6}}{1.6\times10^{-19}}=2\times10^{13}$ excess electrons.

questions.q: A point charge A of $+10\mu C$ and another point charge B of $+20\mu C$ are kept 1m apart in free space. The electrostatic force on A due to B is $\vec F_1$ and the electrostatic force on B due to A is $\vec F_2$. Then
questions.explanation: By Newton's third law, the force on A due to B is equal in magnitude and opposite in direction to the force on B due to A.

questions.q: A uniform electric field $E=3\times10^5\,NC^{-1}$ is acting along the positive Y-axis. The electric flux through a rectangle of area $10\,cm\times30\,cm$ whose plane is parallel to the Z-X plane is
questions.explanation: Since the plane is parallel to the Z-X plane, its normal is along Y, so $\phi=E\times A=3\times10^5\times(0.1\times0.3)=9\times10^3\,Vm$.

questions.q: The total electric flux through a closed spherical surface of radius 'r' enclosing an electric dipole of dipole moment 2aq is (Give $\varepsilon_0$ = permittivity of free space)
questions.explanation: A dipole has zero net enclosed charge, so by Gauss's law the total flux through any closed surface enclosing it is zero.

questions.q: Under electrostatic condition of a charged conductor, which among the following statements is true?
options: The electric field on the surface of a charged conductor is $\dfrac{\sigma}{2\varepsilon_0}$, where $\sigma$ is the surface charge density
The electric potential inside a charged conductor is always zero
Any excess charge resides on the surface of the conductor
The net electric field is tangential to the surface of the conductor
questions.explanation: Since the field inside a conductor in electrostatic equilibrium is zero, any excess charge resides entirely on its surface.

questions.q: A positively charged glass rod is brought near uncharged metal sphere, which is mounted on an insulated stand. If the glass rod is removed, the net charge on the metal sphere is
questions.explanation: Bringing the rod near only redistributes charge on the sphere by induction; once the rod is removed with no contact, the sphere's net charge remains zero.

questions.q: In the situation shown in the diagram [a dipole with charge −Q at A and +Q at B, separated by 2a with midpoint O; a small charge −q is at point p directly above O at perpendicular distance r], magnitude of q $\ll$ |Q| and r $\gg$ a. The net force on the free charge −q and net torque on it about O at the instant shown are respectively [p = 2aQ is the dipole moment]
questions.explanation: At the equatorial point p (r $\gg$ a), the dipole field is $E=\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{p}{r^3}$ antiparallel to $\vec p$; the force on the charge $-q$ is $\vec F=-q\vec E=\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{pq}{r^3}\hat i$ (along $\vec p$). Taking torque about O, $\vec\tau=\vec r\times\vec F=(r\hat j)\times\left(\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{pq}{r^3}\hat i\right)=-\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{pq}{r^2}\hat k$, matching option D.

questions.q: A cubical Gaussian surface has side of length a = 10 cm. Electric field lines are parallel to x-axis as shown [cube with faces ABCD and EFGH normal to the x-axis]. The magnitudes of electric fields through surfaces ABCD and EFGH are 6kNC$^{-1}$ and 9kNC$^{-1}$ respectively. Then the total charge enclosed by the cube is [Take $\varepsilon_0=9\times10^{-12}$ Fm$^{-1}$]
questions.explanation: Net flux = (E$_2$−E$_1$)a$^2$ = (9000−6000)×(0.1)$^2$ = 30 Nm$^2$/C. Charge enclosed Q = $\varepsilon_0\times$flux = 9×10$^{-12}\times$30 = 0.27 nC.

questions.q: Electric field at a distance 'r' from an infinitely long uniformly charged straight conductor, having linear charge density $\lambda$ is E$_1$. Another uniformly charged conductor having same linear charge density $\lambda$ is bent into a semicircle of radius 'r'. The electric field at its centre is E$_2$. Then
questions.explanation: Field at centre of a uniformly charged semicircular arc of radius r is $2k\lambda/r$, which is the same as the field of an infinite line charge at distance r, so E$_1$=E$_2$.

questions.q: A spherical oil drop carrying a net charge q is balanced in still air, with a vertical uniform electric field of strength $\dfrac{81}{7}\pi\times10^5$ V/m. When the field is switched off, the drop is observed to fall with terminal velocity 2 $\times$ 10$^{-3}$ m s$^{-1}$. Here g = 9.8 m/s$^2$, viscosity of air is 1.8 $\times$ 10$^{-5}$ Ns/m$^2$ and the density of oil is 900 kg m$^{-3}$. The magnitude of 'q' is
questions.explanation: From terminal velocity, $r^2=\dfrac{9\eta v}{2\rho g}$ gives $r\approx4.29\times10^{-6}$ m, so $m=\dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3\rho\approx2.97\times10^{-13}$ kg. Balancing $qE=mg$: $q=mg/E\approx8\times10^{-19}$ C.

questions.q: A charged particle of mass 'm' and charge 'q' is released from rest in a uniform electric field $\vec{E}$. Neglecting the effect of gravity, the kinetic energy of the charged particle after 't' second is
questions.explanation: $a=qE/m$, $v=at=qEt/m$; KE $=\dfrac{1}{2}mv^2=\dfrac{q^2E^2t^2}{2m}$.

questions.q: Electrical as well as gravitational effects can be thought to be caused by fields. Which of the following is true for an electrical or gravitational field?
options: Fields are useful for understanding forces acting through a distance.
The field concept is often used to describe contact forces.
There is no way to verify the existence of a force field since it is just a concept.
Gravitational or Electric field does not exist in the space around an object.
questions.explanation: The field concept was introduced precisely to explain how forces act between bodies separated by a distance, without requiring contact.

questions.q: Four charges +q, +2q, +q and -2q are placed at the corners of a square ABCD respectively. The force on a unit positive charge kept at the centre 'O' is
questions.explanation: The equal charges +q at A and C (diagonally opposite) produce forces that cancel at the centre. The forces due to +2q at B (repulsion) and -2q at D (attraction) both act along the same direction, i.e. along diagonal BD.

questions.q: An electric dipole with dipole moment 4 $\times$ 10$^{-9}$ C m is aligned at 30$^\circ$ with the direction of a uniform electric field of magnitude 5 $\times$ 10$^4$ NC$^{-1}$, the magnitude of the torque acting on the dipole is
questions.explanation: $\tau=pE\sin\theta=4\times10^{-9}\times5\times10^4\times\sin30^\circ=2\times10^{-4}\times0.5=10^{-4}$ N m.

questions.q: A copper rod AB of length l is rotated about end A with a constant angular velocity $\omega$. The electric field at a distance x from the axis of rotation is
questions.explanation: In the rotating frame, the electric force on a free electron balances the centripetal requirement: $eE=m\omega^2 x \Rightarrow E=\dfrac{m\omega^2x}{e}$.

questions.q: Electric field due to infinite, straight uniformly charged wire varies with distance 'r' as
questions.explanation: By Gauss's law, the field of an infinite line charge is $E=\dfrac{\lambda}{2\pi\epsilon_0 r}\propto \dfrac{1}{r}$.

questions.q: A 2-gram object, located in a region of uniform electric field $\vec{E}$ = (300 N C$^{-1}$) $\hat{i}$ carries a charge Q. The object released from rest at x = 0, has a kinetic energy of 0.12 J at x = 0.5 m. Then Q is
questions.explanation: Work-energy theorem: $QEx=\Delta KE \Rightarrow Q=\dfrac{0.12}{300\times0.5}=8\times10^{-4}$ C $=800\ \mu$C (positive, since it accelerates along E).

questions.q: Two metal plates are separated by 2 cm. The potentials of the plates are $-$10 V and +30 V. The electric field between the two plates is
questions.explanation: Electric field $= \Delta V/d = (30-(-10))/0.02 = 2000$ V/m.

questions.q: A certain charge 2Q is divided at first into two parts q$_1$ and q$_2$. Later the charges are placed at a certain distance apart. If the force of interaction between two charges is maximum then $\dfrac{Q}{q_1}$ = _______.
questions.explanation: Force $F \propto q_1(2Q-q_1)$ is maximum when $q_1 = Q$ (by calculus/AM-GM), so $Q/q_1 = 1$.

questions.q: A particle of mass m and charge q is placed at rest in uniform electric field E and then released. The kinetic energy attained by the particle after moving a distance y is
questions.explanation: By the work-energy theorem, KE gained equals work done by the field: $W = qEy$.

questions.q: An electric dipole is kept in non-uniform electric field. It generally experiences
options: A force but not a torque
A torque but not a force
Neither a force nor a torque
questions.explanation: In a non-uniform field the two charges of the dipole experience unequal forces, giving a net force, and since the field also varies in direction/magnitude across the dipole, a net torque generally results too.

questions.q: The magnitude of point charge due to which the electric field 30 cm away has the magnitude 2 NC$^{-1}$ will be

The force of repulsion between two identical positive charges when kept with a separation 'r' in air is 'F'. Half the gap between the two charges is filled by a dielectric slab of dielectric constant = 4. Then the new force of repulsion between those two charges becomes
questions.explanation: With half the gap (thickness r/2) filled by a dielectric of constant k = 4, the effective separation becomes r/2 + (r/2)$\sqrt{k}$ = r/2 + r = 3r/2, so the new force is F/(3/2)² = 4F/9.

questions.q: Two spheres of electric charges +2 nC and -8 nC are placed at a distance 'd' apart. If they are allowed to touch each other, what is the new distance between them to get a repulsive force of same magnitude as before?
questions.explanation: Original force magnitude $\propto 2\times8=16$ (units of nC$^2$). After touching, each sphere gets $\dfrac{2-8}{2}=-3$ nC, so new force $\propto 3\times3=9$. For equal force magnitude, $\dfrac{9}{d'^2}=\dfrac{16}{d^2} \Rightarrow d' = \dfrac{3d}{4}$.

questions.q: Three point charges of +2q, +2q and -4q are placed at the corners A, B and C of an equilateral triangle ABC of side 'x'. The magnitude of the electric dipole moment of this system is
questions.explanation: This charge system is equivalent to two dipoles of moment $2qx$ each along AC and BC, at 60° to each other. Their resultant has magnitude $2\sqrt{3}\,qx$.

questions.q: $4 \times 10^{10}$ electrons are removed from a neutral metal sphere of diameter 20 cm placed in air. The magnitude of the electric field (in NC$^{-1}$) at a distance of 20 cm from its center is
questions.explanation: Charge $Q = 4\times10^{10}\times1.6\times10^{-19} = 6.4\times10^{-9}$ C. At $r=0.2$ m (outside sphere), $E = \dfrac{kQ}{r^2} = \dfrac{9\times10^9 \times 6.4\times10^{-9}}{0.04} = 1440$ NC$^{-1}$.

questions.q: If there are only one type of charge in the universe, then ($\vec E$ -> Electric field, $\vec{ds}$ -> Area vector)
options: $\oint \vec E \cdot \vec{ds} = 0$ if charge is outside, $=q/\epsilon_0$ if charge is inside
questions.explanation: Gauss's law $\oint \vec E\cdot\vec{ds}=q_{enc}/\epsilon_0$ holds regardless of the sign/type of charge, giving 0 when no charge is enclosed and $q/\epsilon_0$ when charge is inside; KEA awarded a grace mark to all candidates for this question, likely due to the ambiguous framing.

questions.q: An electron of mass m, charge e falls through a distance h meter in a uniform electric field E. Then time of fall
questions.explanation: Acceleration $a=eE/m$; using $h=\dfrac{1}{2}at^2$, $t=\sqrt{2hm/(eE)}$.

questions.q: If $\vec E_{ax}$ and $\vec E_{eq}$ represents electric field at a point on the axial and equatorial line of a dipole. If points are at a distance r from the centre of the dipole, for $r \gg a$
questions.explanation: $E_{ax}=\dfrac{2kp}{r^3}$ and $E_{eq}=\dfrac{kp}{r^3}$, so $E_{ax}=2E_{eq}$.

questions.q: Two spheres carrying charges +6 μC and +9 μC, separated by a distance d, experiences a force of repulsion F. When a charge of –3 μC is given to both the spheres and kept at the same distance as before, the new force of repulsion is
questions.explanation: New charges become +3 μC and +6 μC (product 18) versus the original 6×9=54; since force ∝ product of charges, new force = F×(18/54) = F/3.

questions.q: Pick out the statement which is incorrect.
options: The tangent drawn to a line of force represents the direction of electric field.
The electric field lines forms closed loop.
A negative test charge experiences a force opposite to the direction of the field.
questions.explanation: Electrostatic field lines start on positive charges and end on negative charges (or at infinity); they never form closed loops, so statement (2) is incorrect.

questions.q: The angle between the dipole moment and electric field at any point on the equatorial plane is
questions.explanation: On the equatorial line, the field is directed opposite to the dipole moment, so the angle between them is 180°.

questions.q: If a charge on the body is 1 nC, then how many electrons are present on the body?

Two equal and opposite charges of masses m$_1$ and m$_2$ are accelerated in a uniform electric field through the same distance. What is the ratio of their accelerations if their ratio of masses is \dfrac{m$_1$}{m$_2$} = 0.5?
questions.explanation: Since a = qE/m and the charges have equal magnitude, a$_1$/a$_2$ = m$_2$/m$_1$ = 1/0.5 = 2.

questions.q: What is the nature of Gaussian surface involved in Gauss law of electrostatic?
questions.explanation: A Gaussian surface is an imaginary closed surface; the flux through it is a scalar quantity, so it is best described as a scalar/imaginary construct — the ambiguity of this wording is likely why KEA awarded a grace mark.

questions.q: A spherical conductor of radius 2 cm is uniformly charged with 3 nC. What is the electric field at a distance of 3 cm from the centre of the sphere?
questions.explanation: For a point outside the sphere, E = kQ/r$^2$ = (9\times10^9 \times 3\times10^{-9})/(0.03)^2 = 27/0.0009 = 3\times10^4 V/m.

questions.q: A small oil drop of mass 10$^{-6}$ kg is hanging in at rest between two plates separated by 1 mm having a potential difference of 500 V. The charge on the drop is ________ (g = 10 ms$^{-2}$)
questions.explanation: For equilibrium, $qE=mg$: $E=V/d=500/10^{-3}=5\times10^5\ \text{Vm}^{-1}$; $q=mg/E=(10^{-6}\times10)/(5\times10^5)=2\times10^{-11}$ C.

questions.q: A uniform electric field in the plane of the paper as shown. Here A, B, C, D are the points on the circle. V$_1$, V$_2$, V$_3$, V$_4$ are the potentials at those points respectively. Then [horizontal field lines pass through a circle; A is the topmost point and B the bottommost point of the circle (both on the vertical diameter), while C and D lie on the horizontal diameter, C on the left and D on the right]
questions.explanation: The circle represents a conductor placed in the uniform field; in electrostatic equilibrium its entire surface is one equipotential, so all four points share the same potential (in particular V_A = V_B and V_C = V_D). KEA marked this question for grace marks.

questions.q: In the uniform electric field of E = 1$\times$10$^4$ NC$^{-1}$, an electron is accelerated from rest. The velocity of the electron when it has travelled a distance of 2$\times$10$^{-2}$ m is nearly ......... ms$^{-1}$ ($\dfrac{e}{m}$ of electron $\approx$ 1.8$\times$10$^{11}$ C kg$^{-1}$)
Acceleration of a charged particle of charge 'q' and mass 'm' moving in a uniform electric field of strength 'E' is
questions.explanation: By Newton's second law, $a=F/m=qE/m$.

questions.q: Two identical charged spheres of material density $\rho$, suspended from the same point by inextensible strings of equal length make an angle $\theta$ between the strings. When suspended in a liquid of density $\sigma$ the angle $\theta$ remains the same. The dielectric constant $K$ of the liquid is .............
questions.explanation: For the angle to remain unchanged, the ratio of electric force to effective weight must stay the same; since the electric force reduces by factor $K$ and the effective weight reduces due to buoyancy, balancing gives $K=\dfrac{\rho}{\rho-\sigma}$.

questions.q: The electric field at a point due to an electric dipole, on an axis inclined at an angle $\theta (<90^0)$ to the dipole axis, is perpendicular to the dipole axis, if the angle $\theta$ is .............
questions.explanation: The dipole field makes angle $\alpha$ with the radius vector where $\tan\alpha=\tan\theta/2$; requiring the resultant to be perpendicular to the axis means $\theta+\alpha=90^0$, which solves to $\tan\theta=\sqrt2$, i.e. $\theta=Tan^{-1}(\sqrt2)$.

questions.q: Two small spheres of masses $M_1$ and $M_2$ are suspended by weightless insulating threads of lengths $L_1$ and $L_2$. The spheres carry charges of $Q_1$ and $Q_2$ respectively. The spheres are suspended such that they are in level with one another and the threads are inclined to the vertical at angles of $\theta_1$ and $\theta_2$ as shown [both threads hang from a common support level, spheres with charges $+Q_1$ and $+Q_2$ facing each other]. Which one of the following conditions is essential, if $\theta_1=\theta_2$?
questions.explanation: Each sphere is in equilibrium under gravity, tension and the same mutual Coulomb force $F$ (Newton's third law); $\tan\theta=F/(Mg)$. Equal angles require $M_1=M_2$.

questions.q: Two identical conducting balls $A$ and $B$ have positive charges $q_1$ and $q_2$ respectively. But $q_1\neq q_2$. The balls are brought together so that they touch each other and then kept in their original positions. The force between them is .....................
options: same as that before the balls touched
less than that before the balls touched
greater than that before the balls touched
questions.explanation: After touching, each ball carries charge $(q_1+q_2)/2$. The new force $\propto\left(\dfrac{q_1+q_2}{2}\right)^2 > q_1q_2$ by AM–GM (since $q_1\neq q_2$), so the force is greater than before.

questions.q: An α-particle of mass $6.4\times10^{-27}$ kg and charge $3.2\times10^{-19}$ C is situated in a uniform electric field of $1.6\times10^{5}\ \text{Vm}^{-1}$. The velocity of the particle at the end of $2\times10^{-2}$ m path when it starts from rest is
questions.explanation: Work done $=qEd=3.2\times10^{-19}\times1.6\times10^5\times2\times10^{-2}=1.024\times10^{-15}$ J $=\tfrac{1}{2}mv^2 \Rightarrow v=\sqrt{2\times1.024\times10^{-15}/6.4\times10^{-27}}=4\sqrt{2}\times10^5\ \text{ms}^{-1}$.
